pages.text: CO2 has no use in this chapter: vent it. Both blocks below only accept $(item)CO2$(), from any face.

$(l)Exhaust$()$(br)A small vent that mounts on any face of a block. It holds $(item)1000 mB$() and vents $(item)10 mB per tick$(), rising to $(item)100 mB per tick$() once it holds more than 700 mB. One exhaust can keep up with a coke oven or a 2x2x5 stove.

$(l)Smokestack$()$(br)Brick, concrete and metal smokestacks stack into a chimney; build each chimney from a single kind. Each block holds $(item)8000 mB$() and pushes its gas into the block above; only the $(item)top block$() vents, $(item)10 mB per tick$(), rising to $(item)50 mB per tick$() when it holds more than 7000 mB. Pipe the CO2 into the bottom block.

A smokestack vents less than an exhaust but stores much more, which smooths out bursts. For raw throughput, put several exhausts on the CO2 line.$(br2)Pump CO2 from the $(item)top face$() of a coke oven and from a $(item)side of the bottom layer$() of a blast stove.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
